contexts.text: The time of evening is as the daybreak before the morning. Explained... As the evening signified the daybreak before the morning, the evening was so often mentioned in the Jewish Church... AC 2323, Explained.
Under Dawn, see this reference, and at TCR 571:2.
In the Spiritual World, this hunger... is the evening, and after it come the daybreak and the morning.
The daybreak and morning, which follow the night, = the first of the Church.
In Heaven there is no night, but only evening, which is succeeded by the daybreak that precedes the morning.
The end and the beginning of these variations (of state) is the morning, and, in special, the daybreak; for then night is ended and day begins.
In Heaven there are evening and daybreak before the morning; but not night.

Daybreak = the obscurity which precedes the morning.
[Swedenborg footnote 1.] Daybreak = a state intermediate between the last and the first.
The last state of the Church is called evening and night, and its first state daybreak and morning.

When a man receives the Lord, by acknowledging Him as His God, the Creator, Redeemer, and Saviour, it is His first Advent, which is called daybreak.
Cockcrowing, equally with daybreak, = the last time of the Church.
The daybreak before the morning, or the cockcrowing = a state of commencing faith and charity.
